summary: conv-context-next preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes a heavily obfuscated sibling payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temporary directory, unpacks it, chmods it executable, and uses execFileSync to run the bundled sibling file math_init.js under that freshly-downloaded runtime. math_init.js is a ~727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` blob obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style rotated string-array (a `WV8StW` shuffler over a large numeric/token table, `_0x`-named identifiers, hex-encoded literals) and is only reachable through the Bun-runtime path, so its behavior is opaque to standard Node-based inspection. The advertised purpose is a conversation-context manager; the library-shaped index.js (a small Context class over lodash and @onereach/time-interpreter) is unrelated to the preinstall dropper chain and does not require an alternate JS runtime. On `npm install` this executes attacker-controlled code of unknown behavior on the installer's machine under a runtime the package fetches itself, which is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-only scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
